findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee used their bare hands to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed chicken that was cooked yesterday in the cookline cooler was not date marked. During the inspection the chicken was properly date marked. The PIC was reminded that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was prepared/opened being day one). Ensure that required foods are always properly date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following require cleaning:

(1) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The accumulation of dust on the hood system.

(2) The debris on the top of the dish machine. 
 
Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed the following in the cookline single cooler lacked date marking: (1) Chicken that was cooked on Friday; and (2) Jug of milk that was opened on Friday. The chicken was date marked and the milk was discarded during the inspection. The PIC was reminded that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was prepared/opened being day one). Ensure that required foods are always properly date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the hood system has an accumulation of dust. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the hood system is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed the containers holding sugar, salt, and cracker meal were not labeled. All foods not in their original container that can be easily mistakably recognized (ex. white powders) must be identified with the common name. The PIC labeled the containers of salt, sugar, and cracker meal during the inspection. Ensure that all easily mistakable foods not in their original packages are labeled with the common name of the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the table holding the coffee machine (to the left of the dish machine) is not sealed to the wall. Since the coffee machinery is attached to the wall the table cannot be easily pulled out for cleaning. The PIC was instructed to seal the surface using caulking or another method. Ensure that the table holding the coffee machines is sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the floors underneath the fryers and grill have an accumulation of grease and food debris. The PIC was instructed to pull out the equipment and clean underneath. An employee began the process of cleaning during the inspection. Ensure that the floors under the fryers and grill are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
